sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `update` and `destroy` fetch a host with `.first` and use it without checking for nil. WHY: A request with a non-existent ID causes `NoMethodError` when `save_host` assigns `host.host = ...` or when `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, returning a 500 instead of a clean 404. HOW: Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound → 404) or guard nil and `render_json_error` / head 404.

WHAT: The migration interpolates values from `site_settings` directly into an INSERT statement. WHY: An admin who previously set `embeddable_hosts` to a value containing a single quote can inject arbitrary SQL that runs with full database privileges during migration. HOW: Use parameterized SQL or escape each host value before interpolation.

WHAT: `record_for_host` queries with `lower(host) = ?` but the table has no index on `host`. WHY: This lookup runs on every embedded request, and as the allowed-hosts list grows it degrades to a full table scan. HOW: Add an index on `host` in the migration, ideally `lower(host)` if the database supports expression indexes, or a standard btree index with case-insensitive comparisons in the query.

WHAT: The fabricator file contents are swapped between `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. WHY: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `:embeddable_host`, while category-related fabricators were moved to `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`, making the file names misleading and breaking the convention that a fabricator file defines the model named in its filename. HOW: Move the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators back to `category_fabricator.rb`, and keep `:embeddable_host` in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`.

WHAT: `TopicEmbed.import` now passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)`, which becomes nil when no embeddable host matches the URL. WHY: Previously the default `SiteSetting.embed_category` was always used; feed polling and import scripts that call `import` directly can now create topics with no explicit category, changing behavior for URLs that do not match a configured host. HOW: Fall back to the uncategorized category or the old default when `eh` is blank, matching the controller's blank-category handling.

In record_for_host, the query uses `lower(host) = ?` but passes `uri.host` without downcasing it. If the stored value or database collation is case-sensitive, comparison semantics become inconsistent and a case-variation host can bypass or fail the allowlist unexpectedly. Normalize both sides consistently: downcase `uri.host` before comparing, and consider downcasing `self.host` in before_validation so stored hosts are always lowercase.

The migration splits the old site setting value on `\n` and inserts each segment directly into SQL. Old values may contain empty lines, whitespace, protocol prefixes, or trailing paths, but the migration bypasses the model's `before_validation` normalization and the format validation. Use `h.strip` to discard blanks and rely on `EmbeddableHost.create!` (or explicitly apply the same strip logic as the model) instead of raw SQL so the validation/normalization callbacks run.

`record_for_host` builds a URI, extracts `uri.host`, and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. The right-hand side is not downcased, so a stored host such as `EvilTrout.com` will be compared as `lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com'` and fail to match. Downcase the extracted host before the query to make matching case-insensitive as intended.

`host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` treats `0` and empty string the same as `nil`. If category id `0` is ever meaningful, it will be silently replaced. Use `if host.category_id.nil?` to test for an explicitly absent value rather than any falsy/blank value.

`update` does `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately passes the result to `save_host`; `destroy` calls `host.destroy`. If the id does not exist, these actions raise `NoMethodError`. Return a 404/not-found response when the record is nil.

The describe block is named 'allows_embeddable_host' but the model method added in this PR is 'host_allowed?'. The test description names a non-existent method, which is confusing and will break navigation/expectations. Rename the describe block to 'host_allowed?' to match the actual API.

The input placeholder is hardcoded English text 'example.com' instead of using the I18n translation mechanism. This bypasses localization and will appear untranslated for non-English users. Add a translation key (e.g. admin.embedding.host_placeholder) and use it here.

The spec added for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only checks that it is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. It does not exercise create, update, or destroy. Those actions could be completely broken and this spec would still pass, so it does not verify the controller behaviour it appears to cover. Add request specs for the actual actions, or at least assert that saving/destroying a host has the expected side effects.

The spec added for Admin::EmbeddingController only checks that it inherits from Admin::AdminController. It does not call show or update, which in this PR return a serialized embedding object. Those actions could be removed or broken and the spec would still pass. Add tests that hit the routes and verify the serialized response contains the embeddable hosts.

The test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' builds a default topic and asserts expandable_first_post? is false. The implementation no longer depends on embeddable hosts, and the body does not configure or assert anything about them; the assertion passes because embed_truncate and has_topic_embed? are false by default. Rename the test to match what it actually checks (e.g. 'is false by default') or make it explicitly exercise the embeddable_host condition and assert the method returns false for that reason.

Both `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. When the id is not found, `update` passes `nil` into `save_host`, which then calls `host.host = ...` and raises `NoMethodError`; `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on `nil`. This produces a 500 error for a missing resource instead of a 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` and is handled by the base controller) or explicitly guard for `host.blank?` and render a 404.

The migration fetches `embed_category` and `uncategorized_category_id` with `execute(...)[0]['id']` / `[0]['value']`. If either setting is missing, `[0]` is nil and the migration fails. Use safe row access (`rows.first`) and provide a sensible default so the migration can run on databases that lack those settings.

The file `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category` fabricators. Swap the contents back so each file defines the fabricator its name indicates.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, so saving a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.
issues.textoGolden: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

WHAT: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError (`nil.sub!`) instead of producing a normal format-invalid result. WHY: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly; any request that omits the host value makes the save raise a 500 instead of returning the `render_json_error(host)` validation response. HOW: guard the mutation, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s` before stripping).

before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) on a possibly-nil host before validates_format_of runs. The controller assigns host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host], so a request without a host key leaves it nil and nil.sub! raises NoMethodError at save time instead of the format validation producing a normal error response. Add a presence guard so validation reports the failure.

issues.descricao: update and destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController fetch the host with where(id:).first and never check for nil, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of not-found.
issues.textoGolden: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: In the destroy action, the nil-host case (line 15-16) would raise NoMethodError. Consider adding a nil check to handle the case where the host is not found.

update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first but never check for nil, then immediately use it (save_host(host) does host.host = ... / host.save; destroy does host.destroy). A stale or already-deleted id, or an interleaving where a concurrent delete removes the row first, makes host nil and the first call on it raises NoMethodError -> unhandled 500. Guard with a nil/404 check before use.

Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

issues.descricao: record_for_host compares lower(host) against the un-lowercased URI host, so mixed-case referer hosts fail to match allowed hosts and embedding is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

The query compares lower(host) to the un-downcased uri.host. A referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches the stored lowercase host, so embedding is wrongly denied. Fix: use where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).

The query compares lower(host) in the database with uri.host, which is not lowercased, so the comparison normalizes only one side. A referer or URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com) will not match the stored host. Compare against host.downcase, i.e. where('lower(host) = ?', host.downcase).

issues.descricao: The migration copies the legacy embeddable_hosts values into the new table without stripping scheme and path, so hosts stored as http://example.com no longer match the bare-host lookup and previously allowed embeds are rejected after upgrade.
issues.textoGolden: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts lines (e.g. http://example.com/123) without stripping scheme/path like the model does. WHY: migrated rows never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which compares bare uri.host, silently breaking previously allowed embeds.

Migration INSERTs raw embeddable_hosts lines with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost normalizes to bare domain (before_validation strips protocol/path, record_for_host looks up by URI.host). Strip protocol and path before INSERT or migrated hosts will never satisfy host_allowed?.

Legacy hosts are inserted verbatim instead of applying the new model's scheme/path normalization. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 remain in the table, while record_for_host compares only URI.host, so previously configured embedding hosts stop working after upgrade. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

issues.descricao: The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, so each file defines the other's fabricators.
issues.textoGolden: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

comentarios.texto: File named category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while Fabricator(:category) was moved to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Filenames disagree with contents — swap contents back so each file defines the fabricator its name states.

The file names and contents are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category), and category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host. Restore category_fabricator.rb to the original category fabricators and put the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

issues.descricao: The migration builds its INSERT by interpolating each legacy host value into the SQL string instead of quoting or binding it, so a value with a quote breaks the statement.
issues.textoGolden: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

comentarios.texto: The migration's INSERT statement uses string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). This is a SQL-injection concern and should be fixed by using parameterized queries or proper escaping.
WHAT: migration interpolates raw host string into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). WHY: a host value containing a single quote breaks the statement and allows SQL injection via site_settings value.

issues.descricao: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.
issues.textoGolden: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] with no guard when embed_category setting/category is missing. WHY: nil[0] dereference crashes the migration and blocks deploy on instances without that setting.
Migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking empty result; missing site_settings row throws NoMethodError and fails migration. Check for nil row.

The migration indexes the first category-query result before checking whether any row was returned. An installation without a persisted embed_category setting, or with no matching category name, aborts migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Check whether the result contains a row before accessing its id and handle missing fallback settings as well.

issues.descricao: The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer sets up any host condition and passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, so its name no longer matches what it tests.

comentarios.texto: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not establish the true-branch preconditions (embed_truncate true, has_topic_embed true) nor control host presence, so it passes regardless of host logic and would still pass if host checking were broken/removed. Set truncate true + stub embed true with no hosts for the false case.

The test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now uses an ordinary built topic without setting embed_truncate or making has_topic_embed? true. It therefore returns false for reasons unrelated to the missing host, and passes even with the new implementation that never checks host availability. If blank-host behavior remains the intended contract, arrange all the other prerequisites before asserting false; if the contract intentionally changed, replace this case with a test of the actual intended behavior rather than retaining a misleading passing test.

The description "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer matches the code. This PR changed Topic#expandable_first_post? (app/models/topic.rb:869) to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the embeddable_hosts condition entirely, and removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` setup from this test. The assertion now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed (false) and embed_truncate is unset, so the name states a cause the method no longer has — rename it (e.g. "is false when there is no topic embed") or set up the precondition it claims to test.

issues.descricao: The 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but the pretender always returns fruit 1, so it asserts fruit 1's colors and would not notice a find that ignores the id.

comentarios.texto: Test requests fruit id 2 but pretender returns fruits[0] unconditionally, so assertions on colors [1,2] never cover fruit 2's color_ids [3]. Make pretender honor :id or request id 1 / assert single-element case to actually verify plural _ids hydration.

This test now requests fruit 2 but expects fruit 1's two colors. The /fruits/:id Pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so the test passes while hydrating the wrong record and would not catch a find implementation that ignores the requested ID. Make the handler select the requested fruit and assert its ID and corresponding colors (fruit 2 has only color 3), or request fruit 1 if testing its two-color hydration is the goal.

issues.descricao: After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.

comentarios.texto: The save callback overwrites the category using categoryId even when the server substituted the uncategorized category for a blank selection. Adding a host without choosing a category therefore leaves its category badge empty, and editing it reads an undefined category id despite a valid category_id having been returned. Resolve the category from the saved response's category_id rather than the submitted selection.

When categoryId is null (the default for a new row, or a cleared selection), the controller saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that category_id. This callback instead overwrites host.category with findById(null), making the displayed category disagree with the saved category. Use the category from the save response or its returned category_id rather than the pre-save selection.

Use the saved response's category rather than overwriting it from categoryId after saving. For a new host with no category selected, categoryId is null, while the new controller deliberately saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that ID through the serializer. This callback replaces the hydrated category with findById(null), leaving the row without its actual category until reload (and reopening edit also initializes from that incorrect relationship).

issues.descricao: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.

comentarios.texto: Host lookup compares URI.host against a stored value that validation explicitly permits to include a port. Saving example.com:8080 succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 produces URI.host equal to example.com and never matches that record, disabling embedding and retrieval for the configured host. Use a consistent port representation in both storage and lookup.

The validator accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host (`example.com`) and compares it to the stored port-qualified string. An accepted and saved host therefore never authorizes its corresponding URLs. Normalize the stored and queried authority consistently, including a deliberate port policy.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The provider event listener that disables permissions on role/client/group removal now runs only when the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. WHY: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is independent (it depends only on AUTHORIZATION), so in V2-only deployments the listener is skipped and stale permissions remain after resources are deleted, breaking the invariant that permissions disappear with their target. HOW: Change the guard to check both features, e.g. `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) || Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2)`.

WHAT: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` and `hasPermission(String)` do not verify that returned `Permission.resourceId` matches the resource being evaluated. WHY: If `root.evaluatePermission` returns permissions for other resources (e.g. a different client or the all-clients resource), the loops will grant access based solely on matching scopes, allowing a permission meant for one client to satisfy a check for another. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission filters on `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`, so the same defensive check should be applied here. HOW: Add the resourceId equality guard inside the permission loops in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission`.

WHAT: `getClientsWithPermission(String)` loads every client resource of type Clients and evaluates permissions for each one. WHY: For realms with many clients this produces O(N) authorization evaluations on every caller such as `AvailableRoleMappingResource`, causing linear slowdown of role-mapping and client-listing operations. HOW: Consider evaluating a single all-clients resource first and returning early when a global grant exists; otherwise keep per-client evaluation but bound it with pagination or cache granted scopes per request.

The Javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.', but the method signature is 'void requireView();'. This contradicts the actual contract and should be corrected to 'Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}.' to match the pattern used by the neighbouring require* methods.

The Javadoc for requireViewClientScopes() says 'Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.', but the method signature is 'void requireViewClientScopes();'. The prose should be updated to 'Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code false}.' to reflect the actual API contract.

The Javadoc says 'Or if the caller has a permission to {@link AdminPermissionManagement#VIEW_SCOPE} the client. For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to {@link org.keycloak.authorization.AdminPermissionsSchema#VIEW} all clients.' However, ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel) only checks canView()/canConfigure(client) and AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW; it never evaluates AdminPermissionManagement.VIEW_SCOPE. The 'Also' wording is misleading because the V1 per-client check is absent in V2.

ClientPermissionsV2 overrides isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel) and setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) to throw UnsupportedOperationException, even though these methods are part of the ClientPermissionEvaluator interface contract. Since MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, callers holding a ClientPermissionEvaluator reference that invoke these methods will break. Either provide a V2 implementation that honors the interface contract, add default no-op behavior to the interface, or update all consumers to avoid calling these methods on V2.

The tests call getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) and .get(0) without checking that the list contains enough elements. If the realm has fewer default scopes than assumed, the test throws IndexOutOfBoundsException before it can verify the intended ForbiddenException behavior. Guard the index access with an isEmpty()/size() check or select a scope safely, and fail with a clear message if none are available.

The ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false), but in the V2 permission path clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, deleting a client will therefore raise an unhandled exception and abort the transaction. The cleanup should either be skipped for V2, or ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled should be a no-op (or properly clean up V2 authorization resources).

In V2 there is no per-client permission toggle, but the client-removal cleanup path in AdminPermissions.java still invokes setPermissionsEnabled(...). Make this method a no-op instead of throwing UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client does not fail when admin fine-grained authz V2 is enabled.

issues.descricao: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup is now entirely wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled the pre-existing removal cleanup (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) no longer runs. Realms using the non-V2 permission model will keep orphaned authorization resources/permissions after a client, role or group is removed. The gate should preserve the old behavior when the feature is off (run for V1), or the V1 cleanup must be performed elsewhere.

issues.descricao: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
issues.textoGolden: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

issues.descricao: Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
issues.textoGolden: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private getEvaluationContext method.
issues.textoGolden: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and has no caller anywhere in the class. Its only possible consumer in the V1 class, `canExchangeTo`, was overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (line 148-150). The EvaluationContext and its overridden getBaseAttributes are built and then never used — remove the method (or wire it into canExchangeTo if token-exchange is meant to be supported).

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() methods says they return true instead of documenting that they throw ForbiddenException.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for `void requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", but requireView() is void and throws ForbiddenException rather than returning a value. It is a copy-paste of the canView() doc and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}", matching the sibling require* methods (requireListClientScopes, requireConfigure, etc.).

The Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The doc describes a boolean return the method never produces; it should state that it throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false, consistent with the other require* methods.

Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

comentarios.texto: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar and its .integration is accessed without optional chaining. WHY: When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws a TypeError, breaking event creation. HOW: Use optional chaining: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar".

WHAT: When externalCalendarId is undefined, the fallback searches event.destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals undefined, which can never match. WHY: updateEvent loses the previous default of event.destinationCalendar.externalId and may call calendar.events.update with an undefined calendarId; deleteEvent falls back to "primary" instead of the intended host calendar. HOW: Fall back to the first destinationCalendar entry, e.g. event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId. The same fix applies to deleteEvent at lines 315-317.

WHAT: Office365 createEvent still has the old one-argument signature and always uses event.destinationCalendar[0]. WHY: CalendarManager now calls createEvent(calEvent, credential.id), and for collective bookings it expects the credential's matching destination calendar to be selected; Office365 ignores credentialId and writes every host's event to the first destination calendar. HOW: Accept credentialId and select the destinationCalendar entry whose credentialId matches, then use that entry's externalId.

WHAT: Lark createEvent was not updated to accept credentialId and still reads event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. WHY: With multiple destination calendars, Lark events for additional hosts are created in the wrong calendar because the implementation cannot select the calendar matching the credential in use. HOW: Update the signature to (event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number) and select event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId).

WHAT: The slug and requestedSlug metadata conditions were inverted from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. WHY: Non-billing/self-hosted instances no longer store the organization slug, breaking routing, while billing-enabled instances store both slug and requestedSlug, bypassing the verification flow. HOW: Restore the original conditions: write slug when billing is disabled and requestedSlug only when billing is enabled.

WHAT: The recurring-event cancellation branch iterates over all user calendar credentials inside a loop over every calendar reference. WHY: For collective recurring bookings with multiple calendar references, each calendar event is deleted once per reference, producing redundant API calls and 404/not-found errors. HOW: Use only the credential from the current reference (the already-resolved calendarCredential) instead of looping over bookingToDelete.user.credentials.

After destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, the code does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError. Add optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`) or explicitly handle the empty case so the fallback does not crash.

The string "Notes have been hidden by the organizer" is written directly into calEvent.additionalNotes and shown to users in calendar events, but it is not routed through the project's i18n system. The existing TODO even notes this. The PR changed the spelling of this line without resolving the localization gap, so attendees/organizers whose locale is not English still see an untranslated message. Replace the hard-coded string with a translated key (e.g., t("notes_hidden_by_organizer")) and add it to the locale files.

The code destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without checking whether `mainHostDestinationCalendar` exists. Since `destinationCalendar` can be `null`, `undefined`, or `[]` per the type, this causes a TypeError for bookings with no destination calendar. Add an explicit guard, e.g. `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar")` or check `mainHostDestinationCalendar` first.

issues.descricao: Claims the optional chaining in mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant because a ternary already checks it.
issues.textoGolden: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

issues.descricao: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
issues.textoGolden: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId` against `null`/`undefined` and matches nothing (the same wrong pattern is duplicated in deleteEvent at lines 315-317).
WHY: When `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` are called without an externalCalendarId, `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` now resolves to `undefined` instead of the host's destination calendar externalId (old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), so the Google API is invoked with an undefined calendarId and the update/delete targets the wrong (or default) calendar or errors.
HOW: Find the destination calendar for the current credential (e.g. by credentialId) rather than comparing `externalId` to the already-falsy `externalCalendarId`, or restore the single fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

Dead computation in the fallback: the else branch runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet it calls `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, comparing every cal.externalId to undefined. Nothing can match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the fallback that previously returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is lost. Match the intended criterion (destination calendar's own externalId/credentialId), not the already-falsy externalCalendarId.

Same dead-computation defect in deleteEvent: the else branch executes only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet the predicate `(cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against undefined and can never match, so calendarId falls through to "primary" and the event is deleted from the wrong calendar instead of the booking's destination calendar. Fix the predicate to use the destination calendar's externalId (or credentialId) rather than the falsy externalCalendarId.

issues.descricao: The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.
issues.textoGolden: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

comentarios.texto: Organization creation no longer assigns a slug when team billing is disabled, while requestedSlug is also omitted in that mode. New self-hosted organizations therefore have neither publication field, and publish.handler rejects them because requestedSlug is missing. Restore the non-billing slug assignment.

WHAT: slug spread condition was inverted from ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && {slug}) to ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {slug} : {}). WHY: organizations get slug when billing enabled and lose it when disabled, opposite of prior contract and breaking slug/requestedSlug pairing. HOW: restore negation for slug branch.

issues.descricao: Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.
issues.textoGolden: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

comentarios.texto: Office365 creation always selects the first host's destination despite being invoked separately with each host's credential. A collective booking with distinct Office365 calendars sends the second host's token to the first host's calendar ID, causing failed or incorrectly targeted creation. Accept the credentialId supplied by CalendarManager and select the matching destination.

Select the destination belonging to the current credential rather than always taking the first array entry. EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination with that destination's credential, while passing the full event array each time. In a collective booking with two Outlook hosts, the second host therefore attempts to insert into the first host's calendar using the second host's token, typically failing instead of creating the second calendar event. Accept the credentialId passed by CalendarManager and match the destination by that ID (or pass a destination-specific event).

Select the destination belonging to the credential passed by CalendarManager, rather than always selecting the first array element. EventManager now invokes creation for each collective host with the full destination array. A second Office365 host therefore attempts to write to the first host's calendar using its own token, causing creation to fail or target the wrong calendar; meanwhile the saved reference records the second host's externalId.

issues.descricao: Claims updateAllCalendarEvents passes an undefined credential to updateEvent when reference.credentialId points to a credential that cannot be found.
issues.textoGolden: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

issues.descricao: The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining after destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`.
WHY: The previous code was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`, which was null-safe; now when `destinationCalendar` is null/empty (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets it to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one) and `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, destructuring yields `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`, crashing the booking creation flow.
HOW: Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` can be `undefined` because `evt.destinationCalendar` may now be null or an empty array (callers such as handleNewBooking pass `: null` / `: []`). The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, but the new line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` to preserve the null-safe fallback.

The Meet-location fallback destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When `destinationCalendar` is an empty array (which this PR now produces in many callers, e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts, the payment webhooks, confirm/editLocation/deleteCredential/requestReschedule handlers all set `[]` when there is no destination calendar), the destructured value is `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, aborting event creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` to preserve the previous optional-chained behavior.

issues.descricao: For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`.
WHY: For a COLLECTIVE event where neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, the evt field is set to `null` (lines 1063-1067), so the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` of the other hosts are dropped and those hosts are never invited — defeating the multi-host support this PR adds.
HOW: Initialize to an array (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing, or default the field to `[]` instead of `null`) so team destination calendars are always appended.

The optional push discards all collected team destinations when the organizer has no destination calendar. A collective booking with configured secondary hosts therefore creates none of their calendar events even though teamDestinationCalendars contains them. Initialize the array before appending the team destinations.

Initialize destinationCalendar to an array before appending collective hosts' destinations. When neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, it is set to null above, so optional push silently discards all the computed teamDestinationCalendars. Hosts with configured destination calendars consequently receive no calendar events.

issues.descricao: Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the previous non-calendar fallback `result.credentialId`.
WHY: For non-calendar results (video events) `referencesToCreate` now stores `credentialId: undefined` where it previously stored `result.credentialId`, so the persisted video reference loses its credentialId; later code that looks the reference up by credentialId (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts:491-502 deleting the video meeting, or EventManager.updateLocation) can no longer resolve the credential and the meeting is not cleaned up.
HOW: Keep the fallback for non-calendar results: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` (i.e. just `result.credentialId` for both branches).

The reference mapping discards credentialId for every video result. createMeeting returns the video credential ID, and handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its reference has that ID, so newly created video meetings are left behind on cancellation. Preserve result.credentialId for video results as well.

Retain result.credentialId for non-calendar references as well. The previous mapping saved the dedicated video integration's credential ID; this change unconditionally replaces it with undefined for video results, losing the association needed to identify the account that created the meeting during subsequent lifecycle operations.

issues.descricao: createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents fetch each missing host credential with a separate findUnique inside the loop instead of one batched query.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop performs a `prisma.credential.findUnique` on every destination whose credential is not found in the cached `this.calendarCredentials` (line 344); the same per-reference DB lookup was added in updateAllCalendarEvents at line 517.
WHY: For collective bookings with multiple hosts this turns one in-memory lookup into up to N sequential database round-trips added to the booking-creation hot path, scaling with host count.
HOW: Resolve all missing credential ids in a single batched query (`prisma.credential.findMany({ where: { id: { in: missingIds } } })`) before the loop and build a lookup map.

issues.descricao: updateLocation stores externalCalendarId and credentialId from updateEvent's result, which never returns them, so calendar references rewritten on location edit lose their calendar and credential and later updates or cancellations misroute.

comentarios.texto: updateLocation now reads externalId and credentialId exclusively from results, but CalendarManager.updateEvent returns neither field. Calendar references produced by location editing consequently lose their calendar and credential routing information, breaking subsequent updates or cancellation, particularly for secondary collective hosts. Return those fields from updateEvent or preserve them from the corresponding booking reference.

issues.descricao: Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

comentarios.texto: The new per-reference loop runs the recurring-series deletion branch for every host, but that branch still iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials and selects the first calendar reference in each occurrence. Canceling all remaining collective occurrences repeatedly deletes the owner's events while leaving secondary hosts' events untouched. For each occurrence, delete the reference matching the current host credential using the resolved calendarCredential.

For cancel-all-remaining recurring collective bookings, delete each updated booking's reference matching the current outer reference/credential. The new outer loop iterates all calendar references, but this inner block still iterates only the organizer's credentials and takes the first calendar reference of each booking. Every outer iteration therefore repeats deletion of the first host's event, while the additional hosts' recurring events remain on their calendars after cancellation.

issues.descricao: Google createEvent picks the target calendar only by matching credentialId, so destination calendars without a credentialId are ignored and events are created on the primary calendar instead.

comentarios.texto: createEvent now picks the target calendar only by matching credentialId. Destination calendars without a credentialId (handled by EventManager's integration-based branch) never match, so events are inserted into "primary" instead of the configured destination externalId as before.

issues.descricao: For destination calendars without a credentialId, createEvent is called without the externalId, so the booking reference is stored with an undefined externalCalendarId.

comentarios.texto: In the no-credentialId branch createEvent(c, event) is called without externalId, so EventResult.externalId is undefined. The booking reference's externalCalendarId, which used to come from evt.destinationCalendar.externalId, is now not stored, which breaks later update/delete targeting. Pass destination.externalId.

In the branch for destinations without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the externalId argument. CalendarManager.createEvent only returns `externalId` when it is passed in, and EventManager now stores `result.externalId` as externalCalendarId, so these booking references are saved with an undefined externalCalendarId. Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument, so the producer returns what the consumer stores.

issues.descricao: When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.
loadUsers forwards raw Prisma error messages to the client in a 400 response, exposing internal model and query details.
loadUsers throws a plain Error for an empty/invalid dynamicUserList, which the catch block converts into a generic 500 'Unable to load users', hiding a client input error behind a server error.

Collective bookings now push every team member's DestinationCalendar row (externalId, credentialId, userId) into evt.destinationCalendar, and since evt is spread into the webhook payload these other members' calendar identifiers are sent to webhook subscribers.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.
In updateAllCalendarEvents the catch block builds an error `message` that is no longer logged or used after the PR removed console.error, leaving dead code.

When updateAllCalendarEvents fails before the calendar references are loaded, its catch now returns an empty array instead of a failed result, so a failed reschedule or location update looks successful to callers.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: checkIfIsAvailable returns true as soon as it finds a matching date override, before checking the host's busy times. WHY: A fixed host with a conflicting booking during an override window is still considered available, so round-robin/collective slots can be double-booked. HOW: Move the date-override validation into the existing `busy.every` check or keep the override guard but still evaluate `busy` before returning true.

WHAT: The working-hours guard sets `end` to the same minute-of-day value as `start` (lines 141-142). WHY: Slots that start within working hours but run past the host's end time are accepted, letting a host be booked outside their availability. HOW: Compute `end` from `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`.

WHAT: The all-day-unavailable override check compares two dayjs objects with `===` (line 114). WHY: Each `dayjs(...)` call returns a new object, so the comparison is always false and a same-start/end override is treated as a normal availability window instead of blocking the whole day. HOW: Use `.isSame()` to compare the two moments.

WHAT: Date-override comparisons in checkIfIsAvailable format dayjs objects that were constructed from a Date without forcing UTC mode (lines 110-111, 114, 118, 123). WHY: Because the dayjs default is not pinned to UTC, the formatted day/hour depends on the server's local timezone, so the override may match the wrong UTC slot or not match at all. HOW: Parse and format the override dates in UTC: `dayjs.utc(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` and use `.utc()` consistently for comparisons.

The test at lines 788-804 asserts only the final UTC time slots, with a comment claiming 'it should return the same as this is the utc time'. Because UTC slot strings are compared against themselves, the test would still pass if the date-override timezone conversion were removed or broken. To make the test meaningful, compare the slots produced with the invitee timezone against the slots produced with a neutral/UTC invitee timezone (or directly verify the override's local boundaries are converted correctly), so a regression in the timezone offset math causes a mismatch.

Line 114 uses strict equality (`===`) to compare two distinct `dayjs(...)` instances. Because each `dayjs()` call returns a new object, the comparison always fails even when the dates are equal. This causes zero-length date overrides not to be treated as unavailable. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare Unix timestamps/ISO strings instead.

Lines 141-142 compute `start` and `end` from the same `slotStartTime`, so `end` never reflects `slotEndTime`. The subsequent check `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore cannot reject a slot that starts within working hours but ends after them. Change `end` to `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`.

The `checkIfIsAvailable` function was changed to also validate `dateOverrides` and `workingHours`, but the call inside the `selectedSlots` block only passes `busy` and `...availabilityCheckProps`. Since `availabilityCheckProps` only contains `eventLength` and `currentSeats`, the new date-override and working-hours checks are skipped for this re-filtering pass. Pass `...userSchedule` (or explicitly include `dateOverrides` and `workingHours`) so the consumer matches the updated contract.

Each date override now carries its own `timeZone` (added in the same PR at lines 411-415 and used by `packages/lib/slots.ts` at lines 211-225), but `checkIfIsAvailable` ignores that field and converts every override with the single `organizerTimeZone` argument. For multi-host events this can map an override to the wrong UTC day. Use `date.timeZone` (falling back to `organizerTimeZone` only when absent) inside the `dateOverrides.find` callback when formatting/comparing `date.start` and `date.end`, and update the `dateOverrides` parameter type to include `timeZone?: string`.

issues.descricao: The working-hours check computes end from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so slots that start within working hours but end after them are accepted.
issues.textoGolden: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — an exact duplicate of `start` — instead of using `slotEndTime`. WHY: the working-hours upper-bound test `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore compares the slot START against the working-day end, so a slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end (start + eventLength) overruns `workingHour.endTime` is never filtered and is reported as available, allowing bookings outside the host's working hours. HOW: compute `const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();`.

`end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so it always equals `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check is identical to the `start` check and never catches a slot that starts within working hours but ends past them. Use `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()` for `end`.

`end` is computed identically to `start` (both from slotStartTime), so the check `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` can never reject a slot on the upper bound. A slot starting inside working hours but ending after workingHour.endTime is wrongly considered available; derive `end` from slotEndTime instead.

issues.descricao: The date-override check compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so zero-length (day off) overrides are never detected.
issues.textoGolden: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

comentarios.texto: This compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with `===` (reference equality), which is always false, so a zero-length override (start equal to end, whole day blocked) never returns true here. Compare timestamps, e.g. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))`.

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separate dayjs object references, so `===` is always false. The zero-length date-override branch is dead code and such an override is never recognised as covering the day; compare values (e.g. .isSame() or .valueOf() === .valueOf()) instead.

The equality check compares two separately created Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, even when the override start and end represent the same instant. The intended zero-length/closed-day rejection is unreachable, and a slot beginning exactly at that instant can reach the dateOverrideExist success return. Compare timestamps or use isSame instead.

issues.descricao: When a date override exists for the day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking busy times, so slots overlapping existing bookings are reported available.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: when `dateOverrideExist` is true the function returns `true` before running the `busy.every(...)` check at the end. WHY: on any day that has a matching date override, a slot inside the override is reported available without checking the host's existing bookings (`busy` is spread via `...schedule`/`...userSchedule`), so a fixed/loose host who already has a booking during the override window is still shown as free — enabling double-booking. HOW: do not return early here; fall through so the override branch only decides whether the slot is inside the override window, and let the existing `busy` evaluation decide availability (e.g. `if (dateOverrideExist) { /* within override, still check busy */ } else { /* fall through to busy */ }`).

The new `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` short-circuits the `busy` conflict check (and the workingHours check) for any slot that falls inside a date override window. Every caller of `checkIfIsAvailable` previously counted on it returning false for a slot that overlaps an existing booking; on days covered by a date override that guarantee is gone, so slots conflicting with the user's real bookings are now reported as available and can be double-booked. The override branch should let control fall through to the `busy.every(...)` check (returning true only for the availability-window part) instead of returning early.

A matching date override returns true before checking busy periods. Both fixed-host and loose-host callers pass calendar and booking conflicts in busy, so a host with an override is offered even when an existing booking overlaps the slot. Continue to the busy checks after validating the override instead of returning true.

issues.descricao: The working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for the weekday excludes it, so split schedules (e.g. morning and afternoon) reject all slots.

comentarios.texto: The working-hours predicate rejects a slot if any interval on its weekday does not contain it. A split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 therefore loses every slot, since each valid slot lies outside the other interval. Require at least one matching interval to contain the full event instead of finding an interval that excludes it.

This search rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours window on that weekday. With split hours of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon window. Check for containment in at least one applicable window rather than finding any window that excludes the slot.

WHAT: Outside-working-hours test uses workingHours.find() returning true if ANY entry rejects the slot. WHY: With split schedules (two entries same weekday, e.g. morning+afternoon) a valid morning slot is outside the afternoon entry, find() matches and the slot is wrongly rejected as outside hours. HOW: Invert logic to accept if ANY entry contains the slot (e.g. !workingHours.some(entry contains slot) => outside).

issues.descricao: The date-override bound compares the slot start, not the slot end, with the override end, so slots extending past the override are accepted.

comentarios.texto: The override bounds reject only non-overlapping slots rather than requiring the entire event to fit inside an override. A fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 10:30–11:30 event generated from another host's availability, despite being unavailable for its final half hour. Accept only when at least one override contains both slotStartTime and slotEndTime; this also avoids rejecting a slot merely because another interval on the same date does not overlap it.

The upper bound checks whether slotStartTime is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override end but finishes after it is treated as available. Compare slotEndTime with the override end using isAfter, so the slot must fit entirely inside the override.

issues.descricao: The override timezone conversion keeps only hour and minute, so overrides that cross midnight in the invitee timezone become inverted ranges or are applied to the wrong day.

comentarios.texto: Timezone conversion takes only hour and minute, discarding day rollover and turning intervals crossing attendee midnight into reversed ranges. A UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30, which buildSlots skips because start is greater than end, removing valid availability. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval across attendee-day boundaries before building slots.

WHAT: activeOverrides are filtered by UTC day (line 206-207) before the invitee/organizer offset is applied (lines 212-224), and shifted hours are not re-bucketed across midnight. WHY: An override that shifts to the previous/next calendar day in the invitee timezone is dropped from the wrong day or applied to the wrong day, so slots show open when the organizer is off (and vice versa). HOW: Filter/bucket overrides in the invitee-local date after applying the offset, or emit split entries spanning two invitee days.

issues.descricao: The new working-hours check does not reject slots on weekdays that have no working-hours entry, so those slots are treated as available.

comentarios.texto: A weekday with no matching working-hours entry falls through to the busy checks and is treated as available when there are no conflicts. In round-robin events, slots generated for a loose host can consequently include a fixed host whose schedule excludes that day. Reject slots unless a working-hours interval on the slot's weekday contains the event, when no date override applies.

issues.descricao: checkIfIsAvailable's date-override check never rejects a slot that starts before the override start (only one that ends before it), so slots partly outside the override hours are treated as available.

The override day is computed with local-time dayjs(date.start) while the slot day is formatted in UTC, so on a server not running in UTC overrides near midnight are applied to the wrong day or skipped.
With several date-override ranges on the same day, a slot is rejected as soon as it falls outside any one of them, so slots inside the other ranges become unavailable.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty columns and empty data when the use-table-widget-visualization feature is enabled. WHY: Widgets with real table results display a blank table instead of the fetched data, breaking the dashboard table visualization for that feature. HOW: Pass the actual fields/result data (e.g., result.data, result.meta, widget.queries[i]?.fields) into TableWidgetVisualization instead of the placeholder values.

WHAT: BrowserReportSerializer makes both age and timestamp optional without requiring at least one, and the cross-field validation messages are swapped. WHY: A report can pass validation with neither age nor timestamp, violating both Reporting API specs, and the returned errors point the caller to the wrong field. HOW: Add serializer-level validate() that ensures exactly one of age/timestamp is present, and fix the messages so the timestamp validator complains about age and vice versa.

WHAT: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results by relying on dict insertion order via zip(error_ids, events.values()). WHY: If the nodestore backend returns results in a different order, omits missing keys, or if any error_id maps to None, the returned ErrorEvent id can be attached to the wrong event data. HOW: Iterate over node_ids and lookup each node_id in the events dict, then map back to the original event_id.

WHAT: get_request_data sorts the error_events list in place. WHY: Callers that reuse the error_events list after calling get_request_data will see it reordered, which is an unexpected side effect and can break downstream logic. HOW: Sort a copy of the list instead of mutating the input.

WHAT: get_environment_info catches the base Exception class and silently continues. WHY: Real failures (e.g., database or nodestore errors) are swallowed and hidden from monitoring, making debugging impossible and potentially masking data corruption. HOW: Catch only the specific exceptions that indicate a missing environment, and send actual infrastructure errors to sentry_sdk instead of logging at info.

The endpoint logs the entire request body (`request.data`) at info level and logs each raw report on validation failure. Browser reports include `url`, `user_agent`, and arbitrary report bodies that can contain page URLs, source file paths, and other browsing context. This exposes potentially sensitive data to logs. Redact or omit the request body/raw report from log messages, and log only non-sensitive identifiers such as report type and validation error category.

The `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` methods check for the presence of the opposite field with `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`. Because `0` is a valid integer value for both fields but is falsy, a report containing `timestamp: 0` with an `age`, or `age: 0` with a `timestamp`, will incorrectly pass validation. Use explicit existence checks such as `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` instead of relying on truthiness.

`_truncate_title` returns `title[:max_length].rstrip() + "..."` when the title exceeds `max_length`. For a 51-character title this yields 50 characters plus 3 ellipsis characters (53 total), exceeding the intended `ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH` of 50. Either reserve room for the ellipsis before slicing (e.g., slice to `max_length - 3`) or ensure the final string is clamped to `max_length`.

issues.descricao: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
issues.textoGolden: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

comentarios.texto: The timestamp/age validators test truthiness and make both fields optional instead of enforcing exactly one field. Reports with both age=0 and timestamp=0, or with neither field, pass validation despite violating the stated mutually exclusive report formats. Enforce field presence and exclusivity in object-level validate using key membership rather than truthiness.

Check key presence rather than truthiness when enforcing age/timestamp mutual exclusion. Both fields permit 0, so a report with age=0 and timestamp=0 passes both validators even though both fields are present; a zero-valued counterpart also bypasses the corresponding check. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` (or object-level validation) and add zero-value tests.

Check field presence rather than truthiness when enforcing timestamp/age exclusivity. A report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes both validators, despite the declared constraint that they must not coexist; with only one zero value, validation is also asymmetric. Use membership checks on initial_data (or object-level validation) and add zero-value mixed-field tests.

issues.descricao: The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.

comentarios.texto: The new validation-failure warning logs `raw_report`, the full unvalidated report object supplied by the caller. This endpoint is public and unauthenticated (permission_classes = (), @csrf_exempt), so the payload is attacker-controlled, and browser report bodies routinely carry sensitive values (CSP blocked-uri/document-uri/script-sample, sourceFile, plus the full user_agent). Logging the raw payload on every validation failure writes potentially sensitive data into application logs; log only the report `type` (or a sanitized/redacted subset) instead of the entire raw object.

Do not attach the complete raw report to the validation warning. Browser reports contain page URLs (potentially including tokens or personal data in query strings) and arbitrary body contents. Any invalid field now causes that entire payload to be emitted at warning level, exposing it in operational logs even where the existing info-level request logging is filtered out. Log the failed field names/report type or a redacted diagnostic instead.

issues.descricao: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids positionally with nodestore get_multi values, but get_multi does not preserve input order (cached items are appended last) and drops missing nodes, so error details get attached to the wrong error IDs.
issues.textoGolden: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values() instead of mapping by node_id, misaligning ids to payloads and dropping/mismatching on missing keys. WHY: assigns wrong title/message/timestamp to wrong error id and yields incorrect Seer logs. HOW: look up each node_id in the get_multi dict (e.g. dict keyed by node_id) and preserve error_ids order.

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` values preserve input order and that all keys exist. Dict values give no such guarantee; missing keys shorten/misalign the zip, attaching the wrong event payload to the wrong error_id. Lookup per-id: iterate node_ids/error_ids and do `events.get(node_id)` instead of zipping with `.values()`.

fetch_error_details pairs IDs to payloads with zip(error_ids, events.values()) where events is dict from nodestore get_multi. Values order need not match IDs and missing keys misalign, attaching wrong title/message to wrong error. Look up per node_id instead.

issues.descricao: The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

comentarios.texto: The new Snuba replay lookup executes even when enable_error_context=false. Every opt-out summary request incurs an unnecessary database round trip and can now fail on Snuba availability even though it only needs recording storage. Evaluate the flag first and perform the replay lookup only when error context is enabled.

issues.descricao: With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
issues.textoGolden: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the `use-table-widget-visualization` branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`, hardcoding empty rows and no columns instead of the actual query result. WHY: when the feature flag is enabled for an org, every table widget renders an empty table and silently drops `result.data`/`result.meta`/`columns`, a functional regression for all dashboard table widgets. HOW: build `columns`/`tableData` from the existing `result` (and `widget.queries[i].fields`/`fieldAliases`) rather than the empty placeholder objects.

In the new feature-flagged branch, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty props: columns={[]} (an empty array, which is truthy for the `columns ?? fallback` logic, so no columns are derived) and tableData={data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}. All the real result data computed above (result.data, result.meta, fields, fieldAliases, eventView) is discarded, so any organization with 'use-table-widget-visualization' enabled gets an empty table instead of the query results.
