Pass the actual result data/columns into the visualization (or keep the old StyledSimpleTableChart) until the widget is properly wired.

With the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature enabled, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty data/meta instead of result.data and result.meta. Every table widget therefore renders empty for orgs with the flag. Fix: pass tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}} and build columns from the fields.

issues.descricao: The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.

comentarios.texto: The documented custom-renderer contract says fallback runs when the callback returns undefined, but `if (cell)` also falls back for valid ReactNode results such as `0`, an empty string, or `null`. A caller trying to render zero or deliberately suppress a cell instead gets the default field rendering. Check `cell !== undefined` here and in the head-cell renderer so the implementation honors the advertised contract.

Use `cell !== undefined` instead of `if (cell)` to select the custom renderer result, and apply the same correction to the header renderer. The API documents undefined as the fallback sentinel, but valid ReactNode results such as numeric 0, an empty string, or null are falsy. A custom renderer returning 0 or intentionally hiding a cell with null therefore unexpectedly renders the default value instead.

issues.descricao: The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

comentarios.texto: The new attribute query key omits the organization even though its query function fetches an organization-specific endpoint. Switching organizations with identical project selections such as all projects and the same date range reuses the singleton query client's prior organization's attribute metadata, including while the new request refetches. Include organization.slug or organization.id in the query key.

Include the organization slug in this query key. The new useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys implementation fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions contains no organization identity. Two organizations with identical filters (particularly the default all-project selection) therefore share this cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attribute names, and concurrently mounted consumers can reuse a request for the wrong organization. Preserve the organization-specific cache identity that the previous endpoint-based key provided.

Include the organization slug or ID in this query key. The query function fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but the key contains only query options. Two organizations with the same project selection (especially the all-projects selection), date range and dataset therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attributes, and overlapping requests can populate the shared entry with the wrong organization's result.

issues.descricao: The UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps doc says only LOGS is supported, although the hooks are also used with SPANS.

comentarios.texto: The new shared prop documentation claims the endpoint currently supports only LOGS, but this PR also uses these hooks with TraceItemDataset.SPANS (for example in TransactionNameSearchBar). Update this comment to describe both supported datasets; as written it incorrectly tells callers that a supported and actively used input is unsupported.

issues.descricao: Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.
dedupedYAxes is now just [yAxis], so its name misdescribes the code.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
BrowserReportSerializer's validate_timestamp/validate_age docstrings claim one of age/timestamp must be present, but the code only enforces mutual exclusion, so reports with neither are accepted.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The catch block increments retryCount for any error in the try block, not only for SMS scheduling failures. WHY: Failures from `prisma.profile.findFirst`, `getBookerBaseUrl`, or other unrelated setup can mark a reminder for deletion even though Twilio was never attempted. HOW: Wrap only the `twilio.scheduleSMS` call and the successful update in try/catch, or restructure so retryCount is incremented only when scheduling itself fails.

WHAT: The deleteMany second OR branch deletes WorkflowReminder rows with retryCount > 1 without filtering by method. WHY: This cron job is scoped to SMS reminders, but the new condition would also delete email or other-method reminders if any future code increments their retryCount. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount branch so both disjuncts are method-scoped.

WHAT: The cron job's deleteMany queries `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` on WorkflowReminder, but there is no index on the new retryCount column. WHY: The OR branch has no method filter, so the planner cannot use the existing `method, scheduled, scheduledDate` index for it; on a large table this can become a sequential scan every cron run. HOW: Add an index on `retryCount` (e.g., `@@index([retryCount])` or `@@index([method, retryCount])`) in schema.prisma and the migration.

The comment says it deletes only past-due scheduled SMS reminders, but the query now also deletes reminders of any method or date whose retryCount is greater than 1. Update the comment so future maintainers do not assume the cleanup is limited to SMS/past-due rows.

The catch block logs the raw `error` object from SMS scheduling. Provider error responses often include PII such as recipient/sender phone numbers and message bodies. Redact or summarize the error before logging (e.g., log only the provider error code and a generic message) to prevent leaking sensitive data into application logs.

The second branch of the deleteMany OR condition (retryCount > 1) does not include method: WorkflowMethods.SMS. WorkflowReminder is shared between SMS and EMAIL methods, so this branch can silently delete email reminders if retryCount is ever set on them. Add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the retryCount branch to keep the cleanup scoped to SMS reminders, matching the comment and the findMany query.

The new `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` branch in the `deleteMany` filter is not restricted to `WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this SMS cron can now delete email/other-method workflow reminders that use the same `retryCount` column. This changes the behavior contract of the endpoint for any non-SMS consumer of `WorkflowReminder` without updating those consumers. Scope the whole cleanup to SMS reminders.

issues.descricao: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
issues.textoGolden: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: retryCount is incremented with a read-value computed at the start of the run (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) instead of an atomic increment. WHY: if two cron invocations overlap (or the same reminder is processed twice before the write commits), both read the same retryCount and both write N+1, so failures are undercounted and the reminder can loop forever without ever reaching the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold. HOW: use `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` so the increment is atomic (the initial read value is then irrelevant).

`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` is a read-modify-write of the value fetched at the top of the handler, not an atomic increment. Two overlapping cron runs both read the same retryCount and both write the same +1, losing an update, so failed reminders can be retried indefinitely and never reach the `gt: 1` deletion threshold. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead of computing from the stale in-memory value (same issue in the else branch at lines 179-186).

Retry counts are assigned from the stale findMany snapshot instead of incremented atomically, both here and in the catch branch. Two overlapping cron requests can each fail scheduling the same reminder with retryCount zero and both write one, so two failed attempts do not reach the deletion threshold and additional attempts are scheduled. Use Prisma's atomic retryCount increment operation in both failure branches.

issues.descricao: The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.
issues.textoGolden: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

comentarios.texto: The comment "//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date" no longer describes the deleteMany below it. After this change the query also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, and that OR branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so non-SMS (email) reminders with retryCount > 1 are now deleted too. Update the comment (or add the missing SMS filter to the retryCount branch) so the prose matches what the code actually deletes.
The deleteMany OR clause deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method.

The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter, unlike the first branch (`method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`). Because `retryCount` is a generic column on WorkflowReminder used by all reminder methods, this deleteMany now permanently deletes every reminder of ANY method (including EMAIL) whose retryCount exceeds 1, even though this cron is only supposed to clean up SMS reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to this branch (or scope the whole where to SMS) so non-SMS reminders are never destroyed.

issues.descricao: The cleanup comment describes only past-date SMS deletion and omits the new retryCount > 1 deletion branch.

comentarios.texto: Update the cleanup comment to describe the new retry-exhaustion deletion branch. It currently says this deletes scheduled SMS reminders whose date has passed, but this OR branch also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, including future-dated reminders and without an SMS restriction. The comment now misrepresents the scope of this destructive operation.

Stale comment: line 28 says 'delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date' but the new OR clause also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method or date. Update the comment to describe both branches.

issues.descricao: The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the catch block performs an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update` while handling the scheduling error. WHY: if this write itself rejects (e.g. the row was concurrently removed, or a transient DB error), the rejection is not caught and escapes the for-loop, aborting the whole cron run so all remaining reminders go unprocessed. HOW: wrap the retryCount update in its own try/catch (log and continue) so a failure to record the retry does not abort processing of the remaining reminders.

This new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` sits inside the catch block, which is NOT protected by any try/catch. If this update throws (e.g. the reminder was already removed by the `deleteMany` at the top of the file during a concurrent run -> Prisma P2025, or a transient DB error), the exception escapes the `for` loop and rejects the handler, so all remaining unscheduled reminders are skipped and the cron request fails. Previously the catch only did `console.log`, so a single bad reminder never aborted the batch and the endpoint always returned 200. Wrap this update in its own try/catch (or `updateMany`/catch-and-log) so a failed retry-count write cannot take down the whole scheduling run.

The new database update inside catch can itself throw when a reminder has been deleted during scheduling. Booking cancellation deletes reminders through handleCancelBooking and deleteScheduledSMSReminder, so a concurrent cancellation followed by a scheduling error now rejects the entire cron handler and prevents the remaining reminders from being processed. Use an updateMany filtered by the reminder ID to tolerate an already-deleted row, and guard errors from retry bookkeeping so they do not escape the per-reminder error handler.

issues.descricao: Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The catch block unconditionally increments retryCount for any exception (profile/bookerUrl/templating/rate-limit/Twilio outage). WHY: Two consecutive cron runs with a transient global failure increment every pending SMS reminder to 2 and the startup deleteMany then wipes the entire future SMS queue, not just permanently-invalid numbers. HOW: Only increment on permanent scheduleSMS failure, or distinguish transient errors from terminal ones before counting toward deletion.

issues.descricao: The new OR arm on retryCount has no supporting index, so the cleanup delete can no longer be fully served by the existing index and may scan the table.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the deleteMany WHERE now uses `OR` between `(method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now)` and `retryCount > 1`, but WorkflowReminder has no index on the newly added retryCount column. WHY: Postgres cannot satisfy a two-way OR using the existing (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index and will fall back to a sequential scan of the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation, turning a previously indexed delete into a full table scan as the table grows. HOW: add an index on retryCount (or restructure so each branch is index-usable), then re-check the query plan.

issues.descricao: The retryCount increment update is duplicated in the else branch and the catch block.

comentarios.texto: The retryCount increment is duplicated in the else-branch and catch.

issues.descricao: SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.
retryCount is not incremented when a reminder has no message or no sendTo number, so such reminders are reprocessed on every cron run until their scheduled date.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The test cleanup references the literal string "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias. WHY: Created identity providers are never removed after the test, leaking state into subsequent tests and the test realm. HOW: Use the actual alias variable in the cleanup closure, e.g. testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove and testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-20")::remove.

WHAT: The second cleanup in the same test method also references the literal string "alias" instead of "idp-alias-20". WHY: The identity provider created for the invalidation scenario is not removed, leaving stale test data behind. HOW: Change the cleanup to reference the actual alias: testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-20")::remove.

WHAT: remove(String) now calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) unconditionally before the existing cache branch. WHY: The delegate database query previously only ran when the alias cache entry was already invalid; it now runs on every IDP removal, adding a redundant round-trip. HOW: Keep the delegate lookup inside the invalidation branch, or derive the login-cache invalidation from the CachedIdentityProvider already fetched in the else branch when present.

The added test testCacheIDPForLogin validates implementation details (exact cache-key presence/absence after create/update/remove operations) rather than externally observable behavior. This soft concern does not cause the test to pass when the behavior is broken, but the test remains coupled to internal cache keys instead of public behavior.

The cleanup lambda references the literal alias "alias" instead of the IDP's real alias "idp-alias-" + i that was just set on idpRep. As a result the cleanup will fail to remove the created provider and may throw, leaving test data behind. Use the actual alias variable or inline the computed alias in the cleanup.

The cleanup lambda again references the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP's alias "idp-alias-20". The cleanup will not remove the provider created in this block. Use "idp-alias-20" in the cleanup reference.

issues.descricao: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.textoGolden: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

issues.descricao: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

comentarios.texto: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.descricao: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

comentarios.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.descricao: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.descricao: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

comentarios.texto: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Tests assert equality between flat Prisma.sql template literals and nested Prisma.sql compositions returned by the service. WHY: The service builds compound conditions by interpolating Prisma.Sql fragments into other Prisma.sql templates (e.g., buildFilterConditions and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition), producing Sql objects whose values array contains nested Sql objects; Jest toEqual compares enumerable strings/values properties, so the flat expected literals will not match the nested actual values and the tests will fail. HOW: Assert on the emitted SQL text instead, e.g., expect(conditions.text).toEqual(expected.text), or use a helper that normalizes Prisma.Sql to its flattened text/values before comparison.

`this.filters.eventTypeId` and `this.filters.memberUserId` are optional `number`s, but the code tests them with `if (this.filters.eventTypeId)` and `if (this.filters.memberUserId)`. A caller passing the perfectly valid numeric ID `0` will be treated as if no filter was supplied, causing rows for ID 0 to be excluded or, worse, included when they shouldn't be. Use explicit null/undefined checks such as `this.filters.eventTypeId != null` or `typeof this.filters.eventTypeId !== "undefined"` instead of truthiness.

buildOrgAuthorizationCondition always emits `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`. When the organization has no child teams, `teamIds` is empty and PostgreSQL cannot infer the element type of the empty array parameter, causing a runtime error. Guard the team branch the same way the user branch is guarded, and fall back to `1=0` (NOTHING_CONDITION) when both lists are empty.

InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for scope "team", but buildTeamAuthorizationCondition assumes it is defined and interpolates `options.teamId` directly into Prisma.sql. Either keep the schema discriminated-union type in the constructor (requiring teamId for team scope) or validate/throw before using options.teamId, so the previous invariant is not broken.

The exported `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` type marks `teamId` as optional, but the `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` and the team-scope authorization logic require it. A caller can pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId`; runtime validation fails, `this.options` is set to `null`, and `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns `Prisma.sql`1=0``, producing empty results with no error. Align the public type with the schema so missing `teamId` is caught at compile time, e.g. replace the manual type with `z.input<typeof insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema>` or use a discriminated union that requires `teamId` for `scope: "team"`.

issues.descricao: In getBaseConditions, the branches for a missing authorization condition are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql.
issues.textoGolden: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

comentarios.texto: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches (returning NOTHING_CONDITION) in getBaseConditions can never execute. Simplify to: if filterConditions, combine it with authConditions; otherwise return authConditions.

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions: authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object (never null, NOTHING is `1=0`), so `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else { return NOTHING }` can never execute. Simplify to if(filter) return auth AND filter else return auth, or make the nothing-case explicit.

WHAT: `getBaseConditions` returns `filterConditions` alone (no authorization predicate) when `authConditions` is falsy (`else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`). WHY: The WHERE clause returned to consumers then contains no ownership/authorization restriction, so a caller using it would return every booking matching the filters (e.g. all bookings for the given eventTypeId/memberUserId) regardless of the requesting user's org/team membership — an authorization-boundary bypass if `getAuthorizationConditions()` ever yields a falsy value. HOW: Always AND the authorization predicate with the filters and fall back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` when no auth predicate exists, e.g. `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;` (or keep the `NOTHING_CONDITION` default when auth is missing).

issues.descricao: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.

comentarios.texto: The rewritten "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test cannot fail if the combination is broken. The fixture creates a single booking that satisfies the auth condition (userId = user.id AND teamId IS NULL) and the filter condition (eventTypeId = eventType.id) independently, so getBaseConditions returning auth-only, filter-only, or the AND combination all yield the same single-row result asserted here. Only a `1=0` result would be caught. Make the data distinguish the two: add a booking that matches the filter but not the auth (e.g. a team booking with the same eventTypeId), then assert the result excludes it, so that dropping either branch changes the returned rows.

issues.descricao: The caching tests for getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions were removed in the Prisma.sql conversion, leaving the cached-condition logic untested.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now extends StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the required abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, or build_occurrence_and_event_data, so Python treats the class as abstract. WHY: Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self) at runtime; any detector whose type maps to MetricAlertFire will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler. HOW: Add stub implementations for the abstract methods (raising NotImplementedError where behavior is still TODO) so the class remains instantiable while the stateful abstraction is being built.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now extends StatefulDetectorHandler but provides no implementation of the abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), making the class abstract/instantiable-only-after-subclassing. MetricAlertFire.detector_handler points directly to it. This is a potential issue, though the TODO comment suggests it is known/incomplete.

In the multi-group test, occurrence_2 construction calls build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH) but group_2 value is 10. The mock builder does not validate the value against the condition, so the assertion can still pass. This is a test-local issue, not a cross-file contract mismatch.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed to inherit from StatefulDetectorHandler but remains a `pass` body, leaving required abstract methods unimplemented (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data). This makes the class non-instantiable. Either keep it as a DetectorHandler stub until the stateful implementation is written, or implement the required StatefulDetectorHandler abstract methods.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, so it does not implement the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data declared on StatefulDetectorHandler. HOW: implement the required abstract methods (or keep a concrete evaluate override) so the handler can be constructed.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but with `pass`, so it implements none of the abstract methods it inherits (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data). The class is therefore still abstract and instantiating it (it is registered as `detector_handler` on MetricAlertFire and is constructed by Detector.detector_handler) raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Before this change it subclassed DetectorHandler and implemented the single abstract `evaluate`, so it was instantiable; the PR makes the metric-alert handler path throw. Either implement the required abstract methods or keep the class free of unimplemented abstracts.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler (an abc.ABC) with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract methods — counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data (detector.py:142-170) — none of which are implemented here. The class therefore remains abstract and cannot be instantiated; Detector.detector_handler's `group_type.detector_handler(self)` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` for the metric_alert_fire group type. Previously this class was a concrete DetectorHandler with an implemented evaluate, so this PR newly makes it uninstantiable. Implement the required abstract methods (or revert to a concrete handler) to satisfy the base-class contract.

issues.descricao: The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.
issues.textoGolden: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.

comentarios.texto: The new occurrence builder accepts `value` but never incorporates or asserts it, so the occurrence tests cannot detect incorrect forwarding of the measured value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. For example, `test_state_results_multi_group` supplies 10 for group_2 but builds its expected occurrence with 6 and still passes. A regression that passes a constant or another group's measurement at the new production hook would therefore go unnoticed. Include the value in the mock occurrence's evidence and use the actual expected measurement, or assert the hook's arguments directly.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value: int` but never uses it (the occurrence is built only from `group_key`/`new_status`), and this same helper is also the implementation of `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because neither the expected occurrence nor the handler output depends on the value, tests like `test_state_results_multi_group` (which incorrectly builds the group_2 occurrence with `value=6` while the packet carries `10`) and `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` (expected built with 6 vs packet 8) pass regardless of the value actually passed into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. If evaluation passed a wrong value, these tests would still pass, so they do not verify the value/threshold path they appear to cover. Include `value` in a field of the occurrence (or assert on it in the handler) and fix the wrong expected values so the argument is actually checked.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts a `value: int` parameter but never uses it — the returned IssueOccurrence is derived only from `group_key` and `new_status`. Because `value` is dead, callers can pass a mismatched value with no failure: in `test_state_results_multi_group` the packet contains `group_2: 10`, but the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `6`. Either use `value` when constructing the occurrence so the test validates the group value, or drop the unused parameter and pass the correct value; otherwise the test silently accepts wrong group values.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but leaves the underlying hash empty, so every method other than `[]` (e.g. `each`, `keys`, `defaults`, `map`) sees an empty collection. WHY: This violates the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks/Hash contract; any future caller that iterates or inspects `I18n.fallbacks` will get no locales even though `I18n.fallbacks[:en]` returns a fallback chain. HOW: Delegate storage to a real Hash by calling `super` in `[]` and populating defaults explicitly, or do not inherit from Hash and instead implement only the small interface I18n::Backend::Fallbacks actually needs (e.g. `def [](locale); ... end`).

issues.descricao: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.
